question:
Hiring-manager round, Walmart Senior Software Engineer (IN4): a coding question to **count the frequency of a character in a very large string**. After giving the simple approach, the candidate was given a hint and asked to explain a **parallel, multi-core solution** and its trade-offs.

The same round also discussed **horizontal versus vertical scaling**, **relational versus NoSQL** database choice, and **Redis versus Memcached**, along with behavioural questions (biggest achievement, mentoring, release manager role).
lookingFor: Can you write the simple O(n) solution correctly and state complexity?
Can you parallelise by splitting the work, merging results and avoiding shared-state races?
Do you see when parallelism does and does not help (overhead, memory bandwidth, string size)?
Do you know the main scaling and database trade-offs?
Can you compare Redis and Memcached on features and use cases?
followUps: Why might the parallel version not give an N-times speed-up on N cores?
How would you do it when the data is larger than memory or sits on several machines?
How would you handle Unicode characters outside the basic plane?
When would you pick Memcached over Redis?
How would you count the frequency of every character at once?
